findings.where: First screen (hero) at both widths: below the supporting paragraph, where the one action belongs, and the nav (Profile, Articles, Blog). The same gap recurs at the foot of the article specimen, which ends on the Download link with no sender's address.
findings.fault: The page gives no way to reach Mark. The first screen has no action at all: no email address, no contact link, and no Contact item in the nav. The parts map lists no mailto or contact link anywhere on the page. The tile's own palette names a pad-yellow 'address strip', and its texture note puts the address 'at the foot of the sheet', but neither appears. The article, where a visitor arriving from LinkedIn lands, also ends with no address.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank or agency officer who has read the line and the World Bank credential and wants to ask Mark about an assignment. They find nothing to click and no address to copy, and must leave to search LinkedIn. The founder would object too: the brief's personal-advisor test requires 'one direct, personal way to reach him' with the address shown, and getting in touch is the page's one action.

findings.where: First screen: the name block and supporting paragraph ("Formerly Lead Lawyer, PPP Group, World Bank" / "I advise multilateral development banks…")
findings.fault: Apart from one former job title, the hero gives no evidence of work. It names no base country or regions of work, and no recent assignment, talk or named body that asked for his advice. A visitor sees who he was, but not where or for whom he has worked lately, or how recently. The newest talk (23 April 2026) exists in the specimen but sits only as a download link deep in an article.
findings.who_objects: A procurement-minded bank officer screening advisors against terms of reference. They judge relevant experience by region and project kind, and need to be sure he has done this work for bodies like theirs, in their region. One past title doesn't tell them that, so they must dig through Profile before deciding to write.
